messages:
marco: Quick heads-up — planning controlled profiler runs on a subset of prod GPU hosts tomorrow to validate kernel-selection heuristics + KV cache behavior under real traffic. need guardrails before we flip this on.

ting: what are we targeting — sampling only or full nsys snapshots? any rough overhead numbers?

alex: short summary from the smoke runs on staging yesterday:
- sampling (nsys lightweight sampling, 1/100 requests): ~1.8-3.2% p95 latency inflation, CPU noise up but GPU timelines look clean.
- intermittent nvprof / full timeline captures (5-10s per request): 40-70% token-walltime inflation, spikes on kernel hot loops (softmax/outliers) when seq_len>2048.
- perfetto-based timeline (host-side) shows KV cache stalls ~12ms when cold; sampling hides these but full trace makes them obvious.

alex: example commands we used:
```
# lightweight sampling (~1% requests)
nsys profile --sample=cpu,gpu --sample-rate=100 --output=lite_trace

# full short snapshot (use sparingly)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cupti,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --duration=8s --output=full_snap
```

alex: TL;DR: sampling gives us hotspots with low overhead, full traces are extremely useful but too heavy for normal prod traffic unless tightly rate-limited.

samira: agreed. propose these guardrails:
1) only run sampling on <=10% of hosts in a rack at any time.
2) limit sampling duty-cycle to 0.5-2% of requests per host.
3) full captures require explicit opt-in and must be rate-limited to <1 capture per host per hour.
4) auto-disable on error rate delta >0.5% or latency p95 delta >5%.
5) tag traces with model, seq_len_bucket, and KV-cache-hit-rate so we can correlate.

marco: love the guardrails. also add: do not run full captures on dedicated customer capacity without approval (compliance).

ting: how do we estimate overhead before enabling? can we simulate heavier seq_len distributions?

alex: yes — synthetic driver that replays production token-length histogram against a staging rack with profiler hooks. two quick metrics to estimate: token-walltime inflation and GPU kernel time inflation. run both with and without KV cache primed to catch cold-hit impact.

marco: operational checklist draft:
- schedule sampling job via infra-runner (will circle back with host list)
- pre-warm KV cache for 10 minutes on sampling hosts before collecting stats
- attach metric monitors: p95 latency, error-rate, gpu-util, cpu-steal
- set auto-disable alerts in prometheus for thresholds in samira's list
- collect and anonymize traces, store in perf-bucket with TTL 14d

infra-bot: scheduled profiler-sampling job: prod-rack-3 hosts [r3-01,r3-02] at 2026-04-03T02:00:00Z. job id: prof-samp-183999. will post results thread when complete. :white_check_mark:

ting: one more thought — kernel-selection changes we recently pushed might shift hotspots. let's tag rollout id and compare pre/post kernel-map so we don't conflate profiler overhead with real regressions.

samira: +1. also include snapshot of batching config (batch size distribution, batching window ms) with every trace.

alex: action items for me: produce a small write-up with the numeric overhead table (sampling rates vs overhead) and example perfetto timelines. will paste here by EOD.

marco: perfect. if anyone sees the infra-bot job fail, @here please pause new profiler runs until we triage. :warning:

ting: thanks — appreciate the low-impact approach. :thumbsup:
